title: What Counts as Money Put Into a Package Whose Deposit Terms Differ
content:
Whether the product returns the deposit on cancellation, and whether components stand priced onto the package ledger, decide what counts as the money the party put into a package sold under Wanderlane's Vacation Package Products. The deposits taken are what the deposit lines on the package ledger come to; the components are the component lines standing on that same ledger.

**Deposit returnable, with components priced onto the package.** Where the product returns the deposit on cancellation and the package ledger carries components priced onto it — 1 or more such lines, coming to more than nothing — the money the party put in is every deposit, every instalment and those components.

**Deposit not returnable.** Where the product returns no deposit on cancellation, the money the party put in is every instalment and every component priced onto the package, the deposits taken being left out of it altogether.

**Otherwise.** Where the product returns the deposit on cancellation and no component stands priced onto the package ledger, the money the party put in is not varied under this note.

## The three cases

| Deposit returnable on the product | Components priced onto the package ledger | What counts as the money put in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | 1 or more | every deposit, every instalment and those components |
| no | any | every instalment and every component, the deposits left out |
| yes | none | not varied under this note |

## Worked on hypothetical particulars

A package with deposits of 2,000.00 USD, instalments of 5,000.00 USD and components of 600.00 USD, on a product whose deposit is returnable: the money the party put in is 7,600.00 USD.

The same package on a product whose deposit is not returnable: the money the party put in is 5,600.00 USD, the deposits of 2,000.00 USD being left out altogether.
